I added the JSDoc block directly above `closeTab` in `<scratch>/agent-opus-ungated--A2-B1-r1/repo/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs`, and `node --test` passes (3 of 3). No code, other functions, tests or other files were changed, and nothing was committed.

I read `src/tabs/PRECEDENT.md` first. The comment agrees with §stable-tab-keys: closing a tab leaves a gap in the keys, and keys are never renumbered. It doesn't suggest renumbering anywhere. I also added the optional note about an unknown key, and I used inline JSDoc types rather than a typedef.

**`git diff`:**
```diff
diff --git a/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs b/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs
index 830a094..9c75809 100644
--- a/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs
+++ b/src/tabs/tab-keys.mjs
@@ -9,6 +9,14 @@ export function openTab(state, title) {
   return { next: state.next + 1, tabs: [...state.tabs, { key, title }] };
 }
 
+/**
+ * Closes a tab. Leaves a gap in the keys (closing `t2` from `t1,t2,t3` gives `t1,t3`);
+ * keys are never renumbered (see §stable-tab-keys in PRECEDENT.md). An unknown key leaves the tabs as they are.
+ * @param {{ next: number, tabs: Array<{ key: string, title: string }> }} state The tab strip state.
+ * @param {string} key The key of the tab to close, e.g. `"t2"`.
+ * @returns {{ next: number, tabs: Array<{ key: string, title: string }> }} A new state; the input is not mutated,
+ *   `next` is unchanged, and the remaining tabs keep their keys.
+ */
 export function closeTab(state, key) {
   return { ...state, tabs: state.tabs.filter((tab) => tab.key !== key) };
 }
```
